nodes.description: A meta-analysis spanning more than 20 million participants found hyperemesis associated with preterm birth before 34 weeks, birth weight under 1500 g, neonatal resuscitation, NICU admission and placental abruption, and inversely associated with macrosomia and stillbirth. The mechanism linking maternal undernutrition to these outcomes was not investigated in that work, so the edge into this node is modeled with unknown intermediates.

nodes.description: A health-system rather than patient-level process, separated from the psychiatric outcome it aggravates because it has a different substrate and a different intervention. Reluctance to prescribe in pregnancy and the inaccurate assumption that the condition is self-limiting lead to women being dismissed and struggling to access care, which leaves the emesis undertreated for longer than it need be. Psychological support does not act on this node; clinician education, guideline adherence and service design do.

nodes.description: Maternal plasma GDF15 rises steeply in the first trimester, and higher levels are associated with vomiting in pregnancy and with hyperemesis specifically. This is the circulating signal that reaches the brainstem; on its own, however, it is an incomplete predictor of severity, because the same concentration produces very different symptoms depending on maternal sensitivity.

evidence.snippet: We confirmed that higher GDF15 levels in maternal blood are associated with vomiting in pregnancy and HG.

nodes.description: GDF15 is synthesized by the feto-placental unit and released into the maternal circulation. Mass spectrometry of a naturally labelled GDF15 variant established that the vast majority of GDF15 in maternal plasma during pregnancy is of feto-placental rather than maternal origin, which is what makes the fetus the source of the emetic signal and the mother the responder.

nodes.description: Antihistamines, phenothiazines and the doxylamine/pyridoxine combination have safety and efficacy data in pregnancy and are prescribed first. They act on histaminergic, dopaminergic and cholinergic inputs to the brainstem emetic circuitry rather than on the GDF15-GFRAL axis itself, which is why they are symptomatic rather than mechanism-directed.

nodes.description: GFRAL is the receptor for GDF15. Its expression is essentially restricted to the area postrema and adjacent nucleus tractus solitarius — the brainstem chemoreceptor territory that lies outside the blood-brain barrier and is the canonical trigger zone for emesis. Receptor engagement suppresses food intake and generates nausea and aversive responses; this is the same axis that mediates anorexia in cancer cachexia, which is why the pharmacology is already well characterized and why blocking antibodies exist.

nodes.description: The organism-level endocrine state produced by the receptor cross-reactivity above, and a concomitant arm rather than the primary cause of the emesis. Suppressed TSH with modest free-T4 elevation occurs in a third to two-thirds of HG patients, and overt gestational thyrotoxicosis in a minority. It resolves with the pregnancy and generally does not require antithyroid therapy — which is why recognizing it as a distinct entity matters clinically.

nodes.description: The defining clinical state: nausea and vomiting severe enough to prevent adequate oral intake. Severity is graded with validated instruments (PUQE, HELP) rather than with ketonuria, which is explicitly not an indicator of dehydration. This node is the convergence point of the canonical GDF15 pathway and the alternative hCG and H. pylori arms.

evidence.snippet: Hyperemesis gravidarum describes nausea and vomiting in pregnancy severe enough to cause weight loss, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, and nutritional deficiencies.

nodes.description: The core supportive intervention. Normal saline with added potassium chloride in each bag, titrated to daily electrolyte monitoring, corrects the volume depletion and the hypokalaemic hypochloraemic alkalosis. Dextrose is specifically avoided before thiamine is given.

nodes.description: The maternal arm of the mechanism, and the reason hyperemesis is not simply a function of placental output. Carriers of rare and common variants conferring low non-pregnant GDF15 are at increased risk of hyperemesis, while women with beta-thalassaemia — in whom GDF15 is chronically elevated from ineffective erythropoiesis — report very low levels of nausea and vomiting of pregnancy. The inference is that the GDF15-GFRAL system desensitizes with sustained exposure, so a woman's prepregnancy set-point determines how strongly the pregnancy-associated surge is felt.

nodes.description: Depression and anxiety scale scores are markedly higher in women with hyperemesis than in controls, and the burden extends to suicidal ideation, post-traumatic stress and termination of wanted pregnancies. The historically assumed causal direction — psychological disturbance causing the vomiting — is not supported; the contemporary reading is that untreated severe emesis, compounded by the care-access failure modeled above, produces the psychological morbidity. This node exists so the association is modeled with its direction made explicit.

nodes.description: Depression and anxiety are markedly more frequent in hyperemesis, and the meta-analysis that established this concludes with a call to build psychological care into hyperemesis services. Treating the psychological burden as a consequence to be managed, rather than a cause to be diagnosed, is the practical corollary of deprecating the psychogenic model.

nodes.description: Sustained inability to eat produces weight loss and micronutrient depletion against the raised demands of pregnancy. Thiamine, with body stores sufficient for only a few weeks, is the critical deficiency; carbohydrate loading in a thiamine-deplete patient can precipitate encephalopathy, which is why guidelines require thiamine before dextrose or parenteral nutrition.

evidence.reference_title: Gestational malnutrition, hyperemesis gravidarum, and Wernicke's encephalopathy: What is missing?
evidence.snippet: Hyperemesis gravidarum (HG), or the severe nausea and vomiting of pregnancy, is one of the most dreaded complications of gestation, affecting between 1.5% and 3.0% of pregnant women.

nodes.description: Body thiamine stores are sufficient for only a few weeks, so sustained vomiting and reduced intake deplete them quickly against the raised demands of pregnancy. The depletion is a metabolic state, distinct from the encephalopathy it can precipitate: it is silent until unmasked, and a carbohydrate load in a thiamine-deplete patient can convert it into overt disease. This is the node that thiamine supplementation repletes, and it is why guidelines require thiamine before dextrose or parenteral nutrition.

evidence.reference_title: The Management of Nausea and Vomiting in Pregnancy and Hyperemesis Gravidarum (Green-top Guideline No. 69).
evidence.snippet: Thiamine supplementation (either oral 100 mg tds or intravenous as part of vitamin B complex (Pabrinex®)) should be given to all women admitted with vomiting, or severely reduced dietary intake, especially before administration of dextrose or parenteral nutrition.

nodes.description: Given to every woman admitted with vomiting or severely reduced dietary intake, and specifically before any dextrose or parenteral nutrition, because a carbohydrate load in a thiamine-deplete patient can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy. This is the one intervention in hyperemesis whose purpose is prevention of an irreversible complication rather than symptom relief.

This is the physiology that drives hospital admission and dictates the composition of replacement fluid — normal saline with added potassium chloride, titrated to daily electrolyte measurement.

nodes.description: The most feared neurological complication. Wernicke encephalopathy arising from hyperemesis carries high fetal and maternal mortality, and its presentation in this setting frequently departs from the classically taught triad, so a triad-based bedside rule will miss cases. It is preventable via the upstream depletion node: thiamine is given to every woman admitted with vomiting or severely reduced intake.
